source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Change a cable reach and distinguish a station for each desk from one station serving every desk, while keeping a selected probe separate.
meaning: The order of quantifiers controls which choices may depend on earlier ones. “Every desk has some reachable station” lets different desks use different witnesses. “Some station reaches every desk” requires one common witness. In both formulas x and y are bound while reach h remains free; selecting one probe desk only evaluates a separate open formula.

definition.setting: Two finite quantifier orders for a one-dimensional distance relation, with a separately assigned free desk probe.
definition.formal_latex: D=\{2,4,6,8,10,12\}\,\mathrm m,\ E=\{1,5,9\}\,\mathrm m,\ R_h(x,y):|x-y|\le h;\quad A_h=\forall x\in D\,\exists y\in E\,R_h(x,y),\quad B_h=\exists y\in E\,\forall x\in D\,R_h(x,y).

signature.x: Desk variable bound in Aₕ and Bₕ.
signature.y: Station variable bound by its quantifier.
signature.φₕ(xₚ): Coverage at the assigned probe desk.
signature.Aₕ: Every desk has some reachable station.
signature.o: Selected quantified formula Aₕ or Bₕ.

conditions: Desk positions are D={2,4,6,8,10,12} m and station positions are E={1,5,9} m on one straight line. Reach h ranges from zero to twelve metres, and Rₕ uses the inclusive distance test |x−y|≤h.
Each desk may use a station without station-capacity, routing or allocation constraints. The model compares distance statements, not a capacity-constrained matching problem.
The free probe xₚ must be exactly one of the six desk positions. Changing it affects φₕ(xₚ) only; it does not control either formula’s bound variable x.
In φₕ(x), y is bound while x and h are free. In Aₕ and Bₕ, x and y are bound but h remains free. Binding x and y does not make these full closed sentences if h is still a variable.
Aₕ is true exactly when h≥3 m. Bₕ is true exactly when h≥7 m, and at h=7 m both stations 5 m and 9 m are common witnesses.
definition.domain_notes: The complete finite grid permits exact checks of these two formulas. A selected probe is an assignment to a free variable, not a new quantifier binding. The module does not parse arbitrary formulas, perform variable substitution or implement a general proof system.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Use desk positions D={2,4,6,8,10,12} m and station positions E={1,5,9} m. The relation Rₕ(x,y) means |x−y|≤h. Aₕ says every desk may choose a station; Bₕ says one station must serve every desk. The open formula φₕ(x)=∃y∈E Rₕ(x,y) has free x and h. Assigning xₚ evaluates one probe row without changing the truth of Aₕ or Bₕ.
grammar.precedence: Preserve the written quantifier order. In Aₕ the existential station choice may depend on the desk; in Bₕ one station is chosen before the universal desk test.

prompts.prompt: Why can Aₕ be true while Bₕ is false?
prompts.answer: Different desks may have different reachable stations, yet no single station may reach every desk.

prompts.prompt: Does selecting desk 2 m instead of 12 m change Aₕ?
prompts.answer: No. It changes only the open-formula probe reading; the bound desk quantifier still ranges over all six desks.
